name: tilelang
description: Domain-specific language designed to streamline the development of high-performance GPU/CPU/Accelerators kernels
one_liner: A simplified programming language for writing the extremely low-level code that makes AI models run fast on specialized chips, without needing years of chip-programming expertise.
buyer: An AI infrastructure engineer at a company training or serving large models who needs faster, cheaper GPU code but can't hire scarce low-level CUDA experts.
business_use_cases: An AI inference company hand-tunes its model's hot-path kernels, cutting GPU compute costs for serving its product.
A hardware startup supporting a new accelerator chip gets working, optimized kernels faster than hiring a dedicated compiler team.
A cloud GPU reseller offers 'kernel optimization as a service' to AI companies, using tools like this to shave compute costs and pass savings on with a margin.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid GPU kernel optimization consulting for AI companies with high inference bills, using this toolchain to deliver faster kernels.

steal_this: This weekend, benchmark one popular open-source model's slowest operation with and without a hand-written kernel, publish the before/after numbers, and use it to land optimization consulting clients.
